answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small time-locked deposit before trading, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then works like an ember that only grows through verified useful work: every honest deal adds a little heat, while detected fraud extinguishes it. One bad actor's loss ripples outward because counterparties share attestations, and a public registry acts as a beacon new agents can check before trusting a stranger. Cost plus shared memory makes fakes unprofitable.
